title: Why Pakistan Tested an Extended Range Version of the Fatah-IV
gist: Pakistan test-fired an extended range Fatah-IV ground-launched cruise missile on Oct 6, 2026, reportedly exceeding 750 km. The text is a truncated teaser covering only specifications and origin, not the 'why'.

insights.claim: Pakistan tested an extended range (ER) version of the Fatah-IV ground-launched cruise missile on October 6, 2026, its third Fatah-IV launch.
insights.speaker: Usman Haider
insights.so_what: Signals continued Pakistani investment in conventional long-range strike; watch the South Asia arms race.

insights.claim: The Fatah-IV ER test missile reportedly flew a range of more than 750 kilometers, making it unique compared with the first two launches; the previous launch was in May 2026.
insights.speaker: Usman Haider
insights.so_what: Extended reach widens the set of Indian targets Pakistan can threaten conventionally.

insights.claim: The Fatah-IV is a byproduct of the 2025 India-Pakistan clashes and was first unveiled publicly at Pakistan's Independence Day event on August 14, 2025.
insights.speaker: Usman Haider
insights.so_what: Shows conflict-driven procurement cycles in South Asia; expect further post-clash weapons development.

insights.claim: The Fatah-IV features terrain-hugging flight to reduce radar detection, a maximum speed of Mach 0.7 and a 330 kilogram blast-fragmentation warhead.
insights.speaker: Usman Haider
insights.so_what: Low-observable subsonic cruise missiles pressure Indian air defense requirements.
